blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Robotic assembly in high-mixture settings requires adaptable systems that can handle diverse parts, yet current approaches typically rely on policies specialized to each insertion task. Although this can reach high success rates, it makes the process of deploying systems for new problems tedious and time consuming. We present a framework for generalizable insertion using world models that combine robot proprioceptive information with raw visual observations captured by a wrist-mounted camera. Our model-based approach trains a single world model on up to 90 insertion tasks with geometrically diverse parts, achieving 56 % \% zero-shot success on unseen objects with unknown geometry compared to just 7 % \% with a model-free baseline. Importantly, performance improves as more objects are included in the training dataset, demonstrating strong scalability. Lastly, finetuning the generalist model on held-out objects significantly enhances data-efficiency compared to training from scratch and, in some cases, achieves better asymptotic performance. To our knowledge, this is the first system capable of assembling unseen objects in an entirely data-driven manner, and thus represents a significant step toward scalable, generalizable robotic assembly systems. † † ⋆ Work completed during an internship at NVIDIA. † † 1 NVIDIA. 2 University of California San Diego. 3 University of Southern California. Correspondence to Nicklas Hansen <nihansen@ucsd.edu> .

blocks.en: I INTRODUCTION
blocks.zh: 一. 导言

blocks.en:
Autonomous robotic assembly [ 2 , 3 , 4 , 5 , 6 , 1 , 7 ] is a challenging yet important research topic in manufacturing and automation, where precise manipulation of diverse objects is needed. State-of-the-art approaches in industry typically rely on hand-crafted controllers
that cannot easily generalize across different object geometries and scene configurations. Existing learning-based systems in research predominantly use specialist policies, requiring extensive training (and often part-specific tuning) for each specific object pair, which fundamentally limits scalability and adaptability. The key challenge in going beyond specialist policies has been the inability of the currently-chosen algorithms to tractably obtain controllers that can achieve both dexterity and generalization.
blocks.zh:
自主机器人组装[2,3,4,5,6,1,7]是制造和自动化领域一个具有挑战性但重要的研究课题,需要精确地操纵各种物体. 工业中最先进的方法通常依赖手工控制器
无法在不同的对象几何和场景配置中简单概括。 研究中现有的基于学习的系统主要使用专家政策,需要针对每一对特定对象进行广泛的培训(并往往进行部分特定的调试),这从根本上限制了可扩展性和适应性. 超越专家政策的主要挑战是,目前选择的算法无法令人愉快地获得既能实现非曲直又能实现通俗化的控制器。

blocks.en: In contrast to current systems, we envision future robotic assembly systems that have the flexibility and robustness required to manipulate new objects with minimal additional engineering, assumptions, or privileged information. To realize this vision, we argue that such a generalizable robotic assembly system demands adaptive control policies as well as robust visual perception capable of inferring detailed object geometry and poses directly from raw visual feedback within a closed-loop control system. While the current paradigms for acquiring learning-based controllers for assembly do not conceptually preclude such a vision, they struggle to scale up the learning of generalist behaviors to large numbers of tasks and rich perceptual inputs [ 1 ] . This begs the question - as opposed to simply exposing methods to more data and compute, does a change in learning algorithm potentially help develop generalist assembly policies more effectively?
blocks.zh: 与目前的系统不同,我们设想未来的机器人组装系统具有必要的灵活性和坚固性,能够操纵新的物体,同时尽量减少额外工程、假设或特殊信息。 为了实现这一愿景,我们争辩说,这样一个通用的机器人组装系统需要适应性控制政策以及能够推断详细物体几何的强视感知,并且直接来自闭路控制系统内的原始视觉反馈。 虽然目前获取基于学习的集成控制器的范式在概念上并不排除这种视觉,但它们努力将通论行为的学习扩大到大量的任务和丰富的感知投入[1]. 这提出了问题,而不是简单地将方法暴露在更多的数据和计算上,学习算法的改变是否可能更有效地帮助制定通论大会政策?

blocks.en: Our research addresses these questions by introducing InsertionWM : a learning-based framework that enables zero-shot insertion of unseen objects with entirely unknown object geometries, using visual world models. Concretely, we develop a scalable, yet data-efficient system for general-purpose robotic assembly that leverages world models trained from raw visual observations captured by a wrist-mounted camera, as well as robot proprioceptive information. Departing from previous work that leverage model-free reinforcement learning (RL) for acquiring robotic assembly controllers [ 6 , 1 , 7 ] , we posit that model-based methods enable more efficient multi-task, vision-based policy learning. Intuitively, a predictive world model yields a dense, self-supervised signal from every transition – decoupling representation learning from the sparse reward – and supports planning at decision time; both are valuable when one high-capacity visual encoder is shared across many tasks, where model-free policy gradients are sample-inefficient and prone to task interference. Doing so allows for training generalist, vision-based policies across wider ranges of problems, without compromising dexterity, a challenge that has proven difficult with prior policy gradient-driven RL approaches to assembly.
blocks.zh: 我们的研究通过引入“插入WM:一个基于学习的框架”来解决这些问题,这个框架能够使用视觉世界模型,以零镜头插入完全未知物体几何的看不见物体。 具体地说,我们开发了一个可扩展但具有数据效率的通用机器人组装系统,利用从手腕式摄像机捕捉的原始视觉观察以及机器人自控信息中训练出来的世界模型。 我们脱离了以往利用无模型强化学习(RL)来获取机器人组装控制器[6, 1, 7]的工作,我们假定,基于模型的方法能够更有效地开展多任务、基于愿景的政策学习。 直觉上,一个预测性的世界模型会产生来自每个过渡的密集、自我监督的信号 — — 从微薄的奖励中吸取分解的表示力 — — 并在决策时支持规划;当一个高容量的视觉编码器被共享到许多任务中时,两者都是有价值的,因为没有模型的政策梯度是缺乏样本效率的,容易干扰任务。 这样做,就可以在不损害灵活的情况下,在更广泛的问题中培训通用的、基于远见的政策。 以往的政策梯度驱动的RL法对组装方法证明,这一挑战十分困难。

blocks.en: Our approach, InsertionWM, learns a generalizable policy without relying on object-specific priors. By training a multi-task policy on as many as 90 90 diverse assemblies from AutoMate [ 1 ] , our method achieves up to 56 % 56\% zero-shot success rate on unseen assemblies with unknown geometry, and we show that performance improves as more assemblies are added, demonstrating strong scaling behavior; see Figure 1 for a summary of results. Lastly, we find that finetuning a generalist model on held-out assemblies greatly improves data-efficiency compared to training from scratch and, in some cases, achieves better asymptotic performance.
blocks.zh: 我们的方法,IntiionWM, 学习一个通用的政策而不依赖于对象特定的前缀. 通过对来自AutoMate[1]的多达90个不同组装进行多任务政策培训,我们的方法在未知几何的未见组装上实现了高达56%的56%的零镜头成功率,我们显示,随着更多的组装被添加,性能得到改善,显示出强烈的缩放行为;结果摘要见图1。 最后,我们认为,从零开始对被搁置的集会进行一般化模式的调整,大大改善了数据效率,并在某些情况下提高了不对称性能。

blocks.en: Notably, the key contribution of this work is not to propose a new algorithm but rather to demonstrate that visual model-based RL algorithms have immense untapped potential for industrial assembly , allowing for much broader and more performant generalist, multi-task policies than previous work. We carefully study the impact of various design choices for such a system, resulting in a practical guide to building general-purpose assembly systems using world models.
blocks.zh: 值得注意的是,这项工作的关键贡献不是提出一个新的算法,而是表明基于视觉模型的RL算法在工业组装方面具有巨大的未开发潜力,因此可以比以前的工作更广泛、更能发挥总论作用的多任务政策。 我们认真研究了这种系统的各种设计选择的影响,产生了使用世界模型建造通用装配系统的实用指南.

blocks.en: II RELATED WORK
blocks.zh: 二. 相关工作

blocks.en: Our work is at the intersection of robotic assembly and RL; this section summarizes prior work in these areas.
blocks.zh: 我们的工作处于机器人组装和RL的交汇点;本节总结了这些领域以前的工作。

blocks.en: Autonomous robotic assembly tasks of interest to the research community often include mating of two distinct parts, with insertion of one object into another being a common yet difficult task due to intricate part geometries, asymmetry, precise control requirements, and the generally small scale of parts to be assembled [ 8 , 2 , 3 , 9 , 4 , 5 ] . Several recent works have explored learning of policies for robotic assembly via simulation environments designed to mimic a real-world setup, and these works demonstrate that such policies subsequently can be deployed on real hardware with limited reduction in performance [ 10 , 6 , 1 , 7 ] . However, due to the immense work required to build such simulation environments, development of better algorithms for policy learning has received comparably less attention from the research community. For example, AutoMate [ 1 ] proposes a system for training part-specific specialist policies to perform insertion in simulation which are then deployed on a real robot setup that closely matches the simulation environment. To do so, the authors curate and preprocess a set of 100 assembly asset pairs originally introduced by [ 4 , 5 ] , and build a parallelizable simulation environment with observation and action spaces that are also accessible in the real world, as well as a shaped reward function that encourages reliable top-down insertion strategies. The authors demonstrate that their system enables training of Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) [ 11 ] via online RL on individual object pairs, and include an exploratory experiment in which a number of learned specialist policies are distilled into a (blind) generalist insertion policy. In this work, we focus on the algorithmic aspect of robotic assembly and set out to develop a learning-based system that can insert unseen objects with unknown geometry in a zero-shot manner, relying purely on raw visual observations from a wrist-mounted camera.
blocks.zh: 研究界感兴趣的自主机器人组装任务往往包括两个不同部分的交配,由于复杂部分的几何美图,不对称,精确的控制要求,以及拟组装的部件一般规模较小[8,2,3,9,4,5],将一个物体插入另一个是常见但困难的任务. 最近的一些作品探索了通过模拟现实世界设置的模拟环境来学习机器人组装政策,这些作品表明,这些政策随后可以部署在实际硬件上,其性能有限度的下降[10,6,1,7]. 然而,由于建立这种模拟环境需要大量工作,开发更好的政策学习算法得到研究界的注意相对较少。 例如,AutoMate [1] 提出一个系统,用于培训特定部分的专家政策,以便在模拟中进行插入,然后部署在与模拟环境密切匹配的真正机器人设置上。 为此,作者对最初由[4,5]推出的一组100个组装资产配对进行校验和预处理,并搭建一个平行的模拟环境,与现实世界同样可以进入的观测和行动空间,以及鼓励可靠的自上而下插入策略的成形奖励功能. 作者证明,他们的系统能够通过在线RL对单个对象对进行近似政策优化(PPO)[11]培训,并包括一个探索性实验,其中将一些学习过的专家政策提炼成一种(盲的)泛性插入政策. 在这部作品中,我们专注于机器人组装的算法方面,并着手开发一种基于学习的系统,可以零拍的方式插入无名几何的看不见物体,完全依靠手腕挂相机的原始视觉观测.

blocks.en: Reinforcement learning for robotics has been of great interest to the research community over the past decade, with applications including tabletop manipulation [ 12 , 13 , 14 , 15 , 16 , 17 , 18 , 19 ] , dexterous manipulation [ 20 , 21 , 22 , 23 ] , and outdoor locomotion [ 24 , 25 , 26 , 27 , 28 ] . A common property of these applications is that they require learning robust control policies that can operate in increasingly noisy and unstructured environments (cannot easily be programmed), yet the tasks themselves are often quite forgiving in terms of precision of motions [ 29 ] . In this work, we focus on learning precise visual policies for assembly of (unseen) objects with unknown geometry, a significantly more challenging problem setting than what RL is typically used for in robotics literature. To achieve our goal, we build upon model-based RL algorithm TD-MPC2 [ 30 , 31 ] , which has been shown empirically to outperform contemporary RL algorithms across a variety of continuous control tasks [ 32 ] . Notably, this is (to the best of our knowledge) the first successful application of model-based RL algorithms in the area of robotic assembly.
blocks.zh: 在过去十年中,机器人的强化学习引起了研究界的极大兴趣,其应用包括台式计算机操控[12,13,14,15,16,17,18,19],dexterous操控[20,21,22,23],室外操控[24,25,26,27,28]. 这些应用的一个共同属性是,它们需要学习强健的控制政策,这些政策可以在越来越吵闹和结构不合理的环境中运作(不可能很容易编程),但任务本身在运动的精确性方面往往相当宽容[29]. 在这部作品中,我们侧重于学习精确的视觉政策来组装(未知)几何学的物体,这是一个比机器人文学中通常使用的RL更具有挑战性的问题设定. 为了实现我们的目标,我们以基于模型的RL算法TD-MPC2[30,31]为基础,从经验上看,该算法在各种连续控制任务中的表现超过了当代RL算法[32]. 值得注意的是,这是(据我们所知)在机器人组装领域首次成功应用基于模型的RL算法。

blocks.en: III PRELIMINARIES
blocks.zh: 三 序言

blocks.en: Setup. We develop a learning-based robotic assembly system capable of high-precision insertion of unseen objects with unknown geometry, entirely from raw visual observations captured by a wrist-mounted camera and robot proprioceptive information. To do so, we leverage Isaac [ 33 ] , a GPU-accelerated and highly parallelizable simulation tool, for iterative data collection and RL. Concretely, our experimental setup consists of (1) a Franka Panda manipulator with a parallel jaw gripper mounted to a table-top on which assembly occurs, (2) a wrist-mounted camera mimicking the common Intel RealSense D435 RGB-D camera, and (3) 200 simulated assets (100 object pairs) for training of continuous control policies. While our experiments are conducted in simulation, the hardware configuration mirrors platforms on which closely related work has been deployed in the real world [ 10 , 6 , 1 , 7 ] . We emphasize, however, that these prior demonstrations rely on low-dimensional pose estimation rather than raw visual inputs; transferring a vision-based world model such as ours therefore raises additional sim-to-real challenges discussed in Section VII . Refer to Figure 1 ( left ) for an illustration of our setup.

blocks.en: Learning a world model with TD-MPC2 [ 31 ] , a model-based RL algorithm that plans actions via local trajectory optimization in the latent space of a learned world model. Specifically, TD-MPC2 learns a latent world model from environment interaction data and leverages Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) [ 36 ] with a learned policy prior as a sampling-based trajectory optimizer during inference ( planning ). All components of the world model are learned end-to-end from data using an optimization objective that combines auto-regressive joint-embedding prediction [ 37 ] , reward prediction, and a temporal difference (TD) [ 38 , 39 ] loss, without decoding raw observations. In this work, we build upon TD-MPC2 due to its demonstrably strong empirical performance on simpler robotic manipulation tasks, and develop a system for generalizable, vision-based robotic insertion. In the following, we provide more details on the TD-MPC2 algorithm as used in our work.
blocks.zh: 学习一个使用TD-MPC2[31]的世界模型,一种基于模型的RL算法,它通过本地轨迹优化一个学习过的世界模型的潜在空间来规划行动. 具体而言,TD-MPC2从环境相互作用数据中学习了潜在的世界模型,并利用模型预测路径综合(MPPI Integrated)[36] ,在推论(规划)期间,先作为基于取样的轨迹优化者,先采用已学到的政策。 世界模型的所有组件都是利用一个优化目标从数据中学习到的端到端,该目标结合了自动递归式联合嵌入预测[37],奖励预测,以及时间差(TD)[38,39]损失,而没有解码原始观测. 在这部作品中,我们基于TD-MPC2,因为它在较简单的机器人操纵任务上明显具有很强的经验性表现,并开发了一个通用的,基于视觉的机器人插入系统. 下面,我们提供更多关于我们工作中使用的TD-MPC2算法的细节。

blocks.en: Dataset for robotic assembly. We base our experiments on the assembly asset dataset proposed by [ 1 ] , which consists of 100 100 geometrically diverse two-part assemblies that themselves are based on previous work [ 4 , 5 ] . Despite significant progress in simulation tools in recent years, making assembly assets simulatable remains a tedious, human labor-intensive task, and thus we limit ourselves to these 100 100 object pairs. We emphasize, however, that our method is not limited to a fixed number of objects and can – without any algorithmic changes – be applied to larger assembly datasets as they become available. The assemblies considered in this work are geometrically diverse and often feature asymmetries along at least one axis. As a result, insertion strategy can vary significantly between objects, necessitating the development of geometry-aware policies. Figure 2 provides an overview of our assets; the plug is to be inserted into the socket .

The plug is similarly randomly initialized and is grasped via motion planning before the start of each RL trajectory. To facilitate learning and improve rate of convergence, we employ a simple training curriculum that adjusts the initial state distribution based on current training success rate. blocks.en: V GENERALIZABLE ROBOTIC INSERTION
blocks.zh: 五. 一般性 Robotic Insition

blocks.en: We present InsertionWM : a learning-based system for zero-shot robotic insertion of unseen objects with unknown geometry . Our framework learns a generalizable world model that at each time step takes robot proprioceptive information and raw depth observations captured by a wrist-mounted camera as input, and outputs delta end-effector pose commands for the robot to execute via planning with the learned world model. Crucially, InsertionWM does not rely on privileged information such as CAD models or object IDs during deployment, making deployment on real hardware feasible in the future. Figure 3 provides an overview of our proposed system. In this section, we describe algorithmic details specific to our problem setting.
blocks.zh: 我们提出IntionWM:一个零射机器人插入不明几何物体的学习系统。 我们的框架学习了一个通用的世界模型,每个步骤都以机器人的自主性信息和手腕架起的相机所捕获的原始深度观测作为输入,输出delta端效应器为机器人提出指令,通过与学习的世界模型进行规划来执行. 关键,插入 WM在部署时不依赖CAD模型或对象ID等特权信息,使得在真实硬件上的部署在未来可行. 图3概述了我们提议的系统。 在本节中,我们描述了与我们的问题设置具体有关的算法细节。

blocks.en: Encoder for multi-modal observations. Previous work on learning-based robotic assembly [ 6 , 1 , 7 ] focus on learning object-specific (specialist) policies for each unique assembly, which does not require substantial knowledge of object geometry beyond what can be deduced through robot proprioceptive information. However, we argue that visual feedback is necessary if we are to learn a single policy (or world model) that can manipulate multiple objects, including objects not seen during training. To this end, we additionally provide our world model with raw depth information from a wrist-mounted camera, and design the encoder h h to consist of three modules: (1) a shallow ConvNet for depth observations, (2) a 2-layer MLP for robot proprioceptive information, and (3) a 2-layer MLP that fuses the two encoder outputs into a single latent state 𝐳 \mathbf{z} , formally defined as h ⁡ ( 𝐱 , 𝐪 ) ≐ h fuse ​ ( h depth ​ ( 𝐱 ) + h prop ​ ( 𝐪 ) ) , h(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{q})\doteq h_{\textnormal{fuse}}\left(h_{\textnormal{depth}}(\mathbf{x})+h_{\textnormal{prop}}(\mathbf{q})\right)\,, (6) where each of h fuse , h depth , h prop h_{\textnormal{fuse}},h_{\textnormal{depth}},h_{\textnormal{prop}} apply SimNorm [ 31 ] normalization to their output. We use multi-modal observations for both our single-object and multi-object world models. As our experimental results will reveal, the addition of visual observations is crucial to the performance of our framework.

blocks.en: Zero-shot generalization. We train both single-object insertion specialists and generalizable multi-object insertion policies via environment interaction. To fully leverage the parallelizable nature of our simulation environment, we choose to train our agents across multiple robotic insertion instances simulated in parallel. When training specialists, we randomly initialize the same assembly with different initial scene configurations across each environment instance, while we maintain one environment instance per unique assembly when training multi-task world models, i.e. , we simulate 90 90 environment instances each with one of 90 90 unique assemblies from our dataset, with significant randomization in scene configuration. This guarantees a uniform distribution across assemblies, as well as robustness to object position and orientation. While providing the model with e.g. a one-hot encoding of object IDs could potentially improve performance on known objects in a multi-task setting, such a representation cannot easily be transferred zero-shot to new objects. Thus, we opt to rely solely on visual information for object disambiguation . Figure 4 shows visual observations captured by our wrist-mounted camera.

blocks.zh: 六. 警告

blocks.en: We validate our approach, InsertionWM , through rigorous experimental evaluation in the setup described in Section IV , including evaluation of both single-assembly specialist policies as well as multi-assembly generalist policies, with our key performance metric being the average insertion success rate across all available assets.

blocks.en: Evaluation. All assemblies introduced in [ 1 ] have uniquely numbered identifiers. We reserve the last 10 10 of 100 100 assemblies (according to their IDs) as a fixed held-out test set with geometries that are still in-distribution but not encountered during training. train generalist world models on the remaining 90 90 objects. All reported test rates refer to these held-out assemblies. When training generalists on only a subset of these objects, we simply select subsets according to their IDs in ascending order. This simple training and test set procedure serves to mitigate any selection bias that might occur from a more manual selection. Generalist success rates are averaged over all assemblies in the training (in-domain) or test (unseen) sets, respectively, and across 100 100 trials per assembly. Specialist policies are trained independently on each of 100 100 assemblies, and we report the mean success rate across 5 5 independent training runs (random seeds) as well as 100 100 trials per run.

blocks.en: Baselines. Our primary point of comparison is AutoMate [ 1 ] , the current state-of-the-art method for robotic insertion with RL. AutoMate trains insertion policies in simulation with PPO [ 11 ] , focusing mostly on specialist (single-assembly) policies with proprioceptive information as input. The trained specialist policies are blind ( i.e. , no visual information) and are not explicitly provided information about object geometry. In addition to these specialist policies, AutoMate also includes exploratory experiments on a generalist policy. This generalist policy is obtained by first training single-assembly specialist policies, and subsequently distilling them into a single multi-assembly policy using a combination of supervised behavioral cloning, DAgger [ 41 ] , and online RL finetuning, while conditioning the policy on point cloud embeddings obtained from CAD models of each assembly. This contrasts with our generalist model that relies solely on raw visual inputs and is trained purely with online RL. Our approach greatly simplifies the deployment pipeline relative to AutoMate: although both use CAD models to build the training simulation, AutoMate further requires per-object CAD at deployment (point cloud embeddings for its generalist and a CAD-based pose-estimation pipeline), whereas our policy acts directly from raw visual observations and needs no object geometry (such as CAD models) at deployment. All AutoMate results are reproduced using the official codebase. Additionally, we compare against a number of variations of our framework , in particular (1) ”blind” world models without visual inputs, (2) world models with an alternative wrist camera placement, (3) world models trained with and without a curriculum that adaptively adjusts initial conditions to be farther or closer to insertion success depending on current training success rate (following the curriculum setting in AutoMate), and (4) a generalist with access to 100 100 expert rollouts (generated by our specialist policies) per assembly. Naturally, access to such expert rollouts during training hinges on the availability of pretrained expert policies, thus severely limiting the scalability of the generalist training pipeline to larger sets of assemblies. The default formulation of our framework thus leverages a training curriculum rather than expert rollouts, and we merely include this additional baseline for completeness.
blocks.zh: 基线。 我们的主要比较点是AutoMate [1],即目前最先进的机器人插入RL的方法. 自动Mate列车在与PPO[11]的模拟中插入政策,主要侧重于专家(单组装)政策,以自主信息作为投入. 训练有素的专家政策是盲目的(即没有视觉信息),没有明确提供有关物体几何的信息. 除了这些专家政策外,AutoMate还包含关于通论政策的探索性实验. 这种通俗主义政策是通过第一次培训单组装专家政策获得的,随后利用监督的行为克隆,Dagger[41],在线RL微调等组合将其提炼成单一的多组装政策,同时对从每组装的CAD模型中获得的点云嵌入政策进行限定. 这与我们的通俗主义模式形成对比,这种模式完全依赖原始的视觉投入,并且纯粹通过在线RL进行训练. 我们的方法大大简化了相对于AutoMate的部署管道:虽然AutoMate都使用CAD模型来构建训练模拟,但AutoMate在部署时进一步要求每个对象CAD(用于其通论者的点云嵌入和基于CAD的姿势估计管道),而我们的政策行为直接来自原始的视觉观测,在部署时不需要对象几何(如CAD模型). 所有AutoMate结果都使用官方代码库复制. 此外,我们比较了我们框架的一些变异,特别是(1) 无视觉投入的“盲目”世界模型,(2) 有替代性手腕照相机布置的世界模型,(3) 受过培训的世界模型,这些模型有适应性地调整初步条件,以便根据目前的培训成功率(按照AutoMate的课程设置)更远或更接近于插入成功,(4) 一个通俗主义者,每集100次专家推广(由我们的专家政策产生)。 自然,在培训期间获得这种专家推广的机会取决于是否有经过预先培训的专家政策,从而严重限制了一般化培训管道的可扩展性,使之仅限于更大的集会。 因此,我们框架的默认拟订利用了培训课程,而不是专家的推出,我们只是列入了关于完整性的补充基线。

blocks.en: Single-assembly specialists. We evaluate specialist policies across all 100 100 assemblies, and report both individual and aggregate performance metrics for our method and AutoMate in Figure 5 . For visual clarity, we order objects from left to right along the horizontal axis according to the average success rate achieved by our approach. Our approach achieves 79.78 % 79.78\% success across all 100 100 assemblies vs. 70.31 % 70.31\% for AutoMate 1 1 1 Reproduced numbers have been verified via correspondence with the AutoMate authors; they acknowledge a slight discrepancy in performance between their paper and released codebase. . While such a substantial performance improvement is to be celebrated, we do observe a decrease in success rates across a few assemblies, e.g. 296 and 726 (visualized in Figure 5 ). We conjecture that this may be due to differences in exploration between PPO (AutoMate) and TD-MPC2 (ours), as well as visual occlusion. Visual inspection of objects for which there is a large performance gap between our method and AutoMate – positive or negative gain – indicates that our approach tends to struggle with large sockets, presumably due to visual occlusion, while our method on the other hand performs significantly better than AutoMate on small, thin sockets. Regardless, these results clearly demonstrate the efficacy of our approach even in a single-assembly case.

blocks.en: Multi-assembly generalists. Our generalist results are shown in Figure 1 ( right ); we report numbers for both in-domain evaluations ( seen objects; left) and held-out evaluations ( unseen objects; right), as well as reference AutoMate numbers obtained from [ 1 ] . We note that the exact training and test splits for AutoMate are not known, but that our experimental setups are nonetheless comparable and that the difference in performance cannot be explained by a difference in training/test splits. It is also worth noting that the AutoMate generalist assumes access to point cloud embeddings of ground-truth CAD models for each assembly (including test assemblies), whereas our method relies solely on raw visual observations. Our results demonstrate that our model-based RL approach achieves considerably better scaling wrt. number of assemblies, achieving a 55.0 % 55.0\% success rate on 90 90 seen assemblies compared to just 15.6 % 15.6\% for AutoMate on 80 80 seen assemblies. Additionally, we find that the zero-shot generalization to unseen assemblies increases with the number of training assemblies, achieving up to 56 % 56\% zero-shot success rate when trained on 90 90 assemblies. This is a significant achievement as zero-shot performance on out-of-domain assemblies reaches in-domain performance at this scale. Based on our observed scaling trend, we hypothesize that in-domain and out-of-domain performances will saturate around this success rate as more assemblies become available in the future, assuming a similar data distribution and difficulty.
blocks.zh: 多集通论者. 我们的一般结果如图1(右)所示;我们报告域内评价(见对象;左)和被搁置评价(见对象;右)的数字,以及从[1]获得的参考自动地图数字。 我们注意到,AutoMate的精确培训和测试分拆并不清楚,但我们的实验设置是可比较的,不能以培训/测试分拆的不同来解释性能的差异。 还值得指出的是,AutoMate通论者假定每个组装(包括测试组装)都可获得嵌入地面真实CAD模型的点云,而我们的方法则完全依赖于原始的视觉观测。 我们的结果表明,我们基于模型的RL方法可以大大更好地扩大规模。 与80个见证人集会相比,90个见证人集会的成功率为55.0%,而80个见证人集会的AutoMate的成功率为15.6%。 此外,我们发现,对隐形集会的零射一般化随着培训集会数量的增加而增加,在对90个集会进行培训时,达到高达56%的56.%的零射成功率。 这是一项重大成就,因为域外组件的零镜头性能达到域内性能的这一尺度。 根据我们观察到的缩放趋势,我们假设,在数据分布和困难相似的情况下,随着今后可以获得更多的组件,域内和域外的性能将围绕这一成功率饱和。

blocks.en: Finetuning a generalist on held-out assemblies. In other areas of robotics and artificial intelligence, one of the most useful capabilities of a generalist is to serve as a pretrained model that can be efficiently finetuned on problem-specific data. This may especially be true in the context of robotic assembly where assembly-specific data is limited. To further demonstrate the value of our approach, we additionally finetune our 90 90 -assembly generalist to each of the 10 10 held-out assemblies; results are shown in Figure 6 . We observe that starting from a generalist model greatly improves data-efficiency on new assemblies and, in some cases, exceeds the asymptotic performance of a specialist learned from scratch (objects 1036 and 1041 ).
blocks.zh: 调整一个关于被搁置集会的通论家。 在机器人和人工智能的其他领域,通论者最有用的能力之一是充当一个经过预先训练的模型,可以在针对特定问题的数据上有效地微调. 这在机器人组装方面尤其如此,因为具体组装数据有限。 为了进一步表明我们的方法的价值,我们将我们的90个90个组装 -- -- 概括地调整到10个被搁置的集会中的每一场;结果见图6。 我们观察到,从泛泛论模式开始,大大提高了新组装的数据效率,在某些情况下,超过了从零开始学习的专家的不对称性能(目标1036和1041)。

blocks.en: Analysis & ablations. We conduct a series of ablations in both specialist (trained on each of 100 100 objects) and generalist ( 90 90 training objects) and report results in Figure 7 . First, we investigate the importance of vision by comparing our approach with (i) a ”blind” version of our method with access to proprioceptive information only, and (ii) an alternative placement of the wrist-mounted camera which provides a better view of the grasped plug but is more prone to visual occlusion. Our results indicate that vision is indeed critical to performance, and our ablation on camera placement corroborates our earlier observation that our approach is prone to failure when the plug is large and (partially) occludes the socket. Our second ablation, shown in Figure 7 (bottom), quantifies the effect of a curriculum that dynamically adapts initial conditions to the current per-assembly success rate. For completeness, we evaluate two such curricula: (i) our default curriculum which starts at the easiest initial state distribution and gradually increases difficulty as success rate increases, and (ii) an inverse curriculum that starts at the hardest setting. Our results indicate that a curriculum consistently improves specialist and generalist performance when evaluated on the full state distribution, while the particular curriculum is less important. We also compare to a privileged version of our generalist that has access to 100 100 expert rollouts (demonstrations) per assembly; we observe that this improves performance marginally but do no adopt this approach for our proposed generalist training pipeline as it scales poorly with larger object datasets due to the assumption of trained experts.
blocks.zh: 分析与分析。 我们用专家(培训100个对象中的每一个)和一般学者(90 90个训练对象)进行一系列的模拟,并在图7中报告结果。 首先,我们调查视觉的重要性,将我们的方法与(一) 仅能获取自制信息的“盲”版方法进行比较,(二) 手腕式摄像机的替代位置,它能更好地观察被抓住的插头,但更容易被视觉隔离。 我们的结果显示,远见对业绩确实至关重要,我们对摄像机放置的淡化证实了我们早先的观察,即当插头很大,并且(部分)堵住插头时,我们的方法容易失败。 如图7(下方)所示,我们的第二次衰退将课程的效果量化,该课程能动态地使初始条件适应目前的每组成功率。 为了完整起见,我们评价两个这样的课程:(一) 我们的默认课程,从最简单的初始状态分配开始,并随着成功率的上升而逐渐增加难度;(二) 从最困难的环境开始的逆向课程。 我们的结果显示,课程在全州分布得到评价时,不断提高专家和通才的成绩,而特定课程则不那么重要。 我们还比较了我国通论者的一个特权版本,即每组有100个专家推出(演示);我们注意到,这略微改进了业绩,但对于我们提议的通论培训程序却不采用这种方法,因为由于假定有训练有素的专家,它与较大的对象数据集相比规模差。

blocks.en: VII CONCLUSION
blocks.zh: 七、结 论

blocks.en: We present a learning-based system for zero-shot robotic insertion of unseen objects with unknown geometry . Our approach achieves substantially better scaling than previous work, with task success rates improving as training data increases. Notably, it achieves an average 56 % 56\% zero-shot success rate on held-out tasks when trained on 90 90 insertion tasks (objects). However, several opportunities for improvement remain; some are discussed in Section VI-B and we further emphasize the following ones: (i) we observe that our system performs poorly on assemblies with significant visual occlusion, (ii) we observe a slight decline in in-domain performance as number of training objects increases, (iii) there is currently limited availability of assembly datasets for training generalists, and (iv) deployment of visual policies on real hardware is still challenging due to potential simulation-to-real discrepancies, inaccurate depth sensing for small objects, and the need for real-time processing of visual inputs. Unlike prior systems that transfer to hardware via low-dimensional pose estimation and model-free policies [ 6 , 1 , 7 ] , a vision-based, model-based approach such as ours faces added hurdles: commodity depth is noisy with blurred edges on small parts, and contact is hard to simulate faithfully. Although we already randomize initial poses, broader pose generalization and active perception that reduces geometric uncertainty before acting ( e.g. Fabrica [ 42 ] ) are promising directions. We believe that future research in any of the aforementioned directions has immense potential in the area of robotic assembly.
blocks.zh: 我们提出一个基于学习的系统,用于零镜头机器人插入不明几何物体。 我们的方法比以前的工作大得多,随着培训数据的增加,任务成功率有所提高。 值得注意的是,在90项90项插入任务(对象)的培训中,被搁置任务的平均成功率为56%。 但是,仍有一些改进的机会;在第六节B节中讨论了一些机会,我们进一步强调以下机会:(一) 我们注意到我们的系统在具有显著视觉屏蔽的组件上表现不佳;(二)随着训练物体数量的增加,我们观察到域内性能略有下降;(三)目前用于训练通才的组装数据集有限;(四)由于可能的模拟-实际差异、小物体的深度感知不准确以及对视觉投入进行实时处理的需要,实际硬件上的视觉政策的部署仍然具有挑战性。 与以前通过低维向硬件转移的系统形成估计和无模型政策[6, 1, 7]不同,一种基于视觉,基于模型的方法,比如我们的面孔增加了障碍:商品深度在小部分有模糊的边缘,而接触很难忠实地模拟. 虽然我们已经随机化了初始构型,但广义的概括和主动感知在行动前会减少几何不确定性(例如Fabrica[42])是很有希望的方向. 我们认为,今后在上述任何方向的研究在机器人组装领域都具有巨大潜力。
